name: The Stillwater Broadcast — Adisa Reinholt's Last Feed
creator: Adisa Reinholt-Mwangi (independent journalist)
description: On March 14, 2207, journalist Adisa Reinholt-Mwangi broadcast live via pirate neural feed for eleven uninterrupted hours from inside a Tier 1 water reclamation facility that HelixCorp had secretly decommissioned while still billing residents. The feed, which reached an estimated 4.1 million simultaneous neural connections before being severed, showed families drinking gray-water runoff and children with chemical burns. Reinholt-Mwangi was arrested at 11:47 PM; the feed cut to static mid-sentence and never resumed.
medium: pirate neural feed, later archived on physical drives
cultural_impact: Triggered the largest spontaneous street action in Meridian 88 history and forced HelixCorp to issue its first public apology in forty years; the phrase 'eleven hours' became shorthand for speaking truth until silenced.
controversy: HelixCorp successfully prosecuted Reinholt-Mwangi under the Meridian Information Sovereignty Act; supporters claim the charges were fabricated. The archived feed is technically illegal to redistribute.
story_hooks: A character discovers one of the original archived physical drives containing the uncut eleven-hour feed — including forty minutes never publicly seen.
Reinholt-Mwangi was released from detention in 2209 and has not been heard from since; someone has been using their journalist credentials.
A HelixCorp internal document surfaces suggesting the decommissioning was not negligence but deliberate population management.
